equation_role.value: Computes the density of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel from the mass fractions of Al, C and Mn.

model_note.value: ρ = 8.15 − 0.101·ω(Al) − 0.41·ω(C) − 0.0085·ω(Mn); ω(Al), ω(C) and ω(Mn) are the mass fractions of Al, C and Mn. C content plays the most significant role in reducing density, but the density of Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is mainly related to Al and Mn contents.

interface_notes.value: During the subsequent cooling process after hot rolling, κ-carbide will precipitate along the δ-ferrite grain boundary if the cooling rate is slow. Al content can significantly influence the crystal structures of the matrix phases.

phase_evolution.value: Due to the difference in Al content, the disordered FeAl phase with A2, the ordered FeAl phase with B2, or the ordered Fe3Al phase with DO3 structures can act as the matrix phases of single ferrite Fe-Mn-Al-C steel. When Al content reaches 6 wt%, the κ phase with a short-range ordering crystal structure gradually forms.

slip_behavior.value: In single ferrite Fe-Mn-Al-C steels the shear of mobile dislocations on ordered phases and dislocation slips mainly control the strain hardening. As Al content increases to 11-19 wt%, the number of active mobile dislocations decreases under low deformation temperature due to a limited number of dislocation slip systems; after fracture, dense dislocation bundles and undeformed B2 phase were observed in ferrite, indicating uneven plastic deformation.

processing_steps_notes.value: Hot-rolled to 2-5 mm thickness between 1100 and 850 °C; in some cases reheating among different rolling-passes is needed to avoid crack generation during hot rolling. A large rolling reduction can provide enough recrystallization driving force, thus inhibiting the segregation of FeAl. For single ferrite steel, a high Al content raises the ferrite recrystallization temperature so the δ-ferrite grains are hard to refine, and δ-ferrite elongates along the rolling direction into banded morphology.
